_comment: Rules for THIS project only. All five kit example rules were deleted. Each rule below maps to a hard invariant in CLAUDE.md and was verified to produce ZERO false positives against the tree at 0514e55 before being enabled. Scope narrowly: a guard that fires on files it shouldn't gets bypassed, and a bypassed guard enforces nothing.

rules.name: no-hand-edited-build-output
rules._comment: INVARIANT I1. Blocks ANY write to a minified file under src/. The guard is a forbidden-pattern engine, so 'this file may not be written at all' is expressed as a pattern matching any non-whitespace character. Covers both npm-generated twins and src/js/vendor/three.min.js — a hand-edited vendored library is the same defect as a hand-edited build artifact. Scope is exactly two directories and exactly two extensions.
rules.invariant: Minified files under src/ are generated or vendored — never hand-edited. Edit the source and run `npm run build`; for vendored files, replace the whole file from upstream.

forbidden.reason: this file is build output or a vendored library — edit the source in src/ and run `npm run build`, or replace a vendored file wholesale from upstream

rules.name: universe-boundary-single-key
rules._comment: INVARIANT I2. The ONLY state crossing the universe/ boundary is the bgAudioMuted localStorage key. comment_style is 'none' so inline <script> blocks inside .html are scanned raw and string literals stay visible — the key name is the thing being matched. Verified: universe/ contains exactly two storage calls today, both bgAudioMuted, both pass.
rules.invariant: universe/ shares exactly one piece of state with the main site: the bgAudioMuted localStorage key. No other key, no sessionStorage, no cookies.

forbidden.reason: localStorage key other than bgAudioMuted — that key is the single documented cross-boundary mechanism (CLAUDE.md, invariant I2)
sessionStorage in universe/ — cross-boundary state must go through bgAudioMuted only
cookies in universe/ — cross-boundary state must go through bgAudioMuted only

rules.name: no-absolute-root-paths
rules._comment: INVARIANT I3. Relative-path convention. An absolute-root path renders fine on the live domain but breaks local file:// preview and every relative-path assumption in the repo, so it fails silently in exactly the place nobody checks. Preventive: zero occurrences exist today. The negative lookahead lets protocol-relative //host through to be judged by CSP, not by this rule.
rules.invariant: Asset paths are relative — ../../assets/, ../css/, ../js/ from src/pages/. No absolute-root paths (CLAUDE.md, invariant I3).

forbidden.reason: absolute-root path — use a relative path; `npm run check:site` is what catches the breakage otherwise
